messages:
Tomas: heads-up — seeing p99 generation latency jump in lon POP right after the 03:10 deploy. p50 ~120ms, p99 ~1.4s, throughput down ~30%.
SRE-Jen: link to the grafana panel? rough host count affected?
Tomas: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rtp/lon-pop?panel=5 — looks like ~18/42 hosts hit the tail. spike starts 03:09:50 and peaks 03:11:30.
Ops-bot: ALERT: lon-pop latency p99 > 1s (03:10) — incident created #inc-4821.
Maya: was there a kernel selector or batching tweak in this deploy?
Deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T03:08Z -> runtime-service @commit a7c9f2d. Release notes: "kernel-selector: enable dynamic fallback; batching: enable aggressive batching when kv_miss_rate > 0.25; kvcache: lower soft-evict threshold"
Raj: grabbed perf profile from a hit host (03:11). KV cache eviction rate spiked at 03:09:58 -> 03:12:10, hit rate dropped from 94% -> 15%.
Raj: ```
kv_stats: {
  total_lookups: 1_200_321,
  hits: 180_048,
  misses: 1_020_273,
  evictions: 76_912
}
latency_pct: p50=130ms p95=420ms p99=1.38s
```
Alina: logs show kernel-selector bouncing between fast64 and fallback_slow on the same host every 200-800ms. example: "selector: switching kernel fast64 -> fallback_slow (latency_crit)"
Henri: the new batch heuristic increases max_batch_delay_ms to 25ms when kv_miss_ratio > 0.25. That increases request coalescing but amplifies tail when misses spike and KV misses serialize.
Maya: so two factors: upstream networking churn causing cross-host miss pattern + new heuristics that enlarge batches on miss storms -> bigger latency tail.
Tomas: can we try pinning kernel to fast64 and lower max_delay_ms on a small canary? thinking: force-kernel=fast64 and runtime.batch.max_delay_ms=8
Raj: ran a micro rollback on 2 hosts (config override) at 03:22:12, pinned kernel + max_delay_ms=8. Can confirm p99 on those hosts dropped from 1.2s -> 160ms within 90s.
Tomas: command used: ``redwoodctl config set --pop lon --filter hosts="lon-pop-canary-1,lon-pop-canary-2" --set runtime.batch.max_delay_ms=8 --set runtime.kernel.force=fast64 --reason "hotfix kv miss amplification"``
SRE-Jen: provider status shows BGP ECMP rebalancing in region at 03:09-03:13 — likely increased cross-host key locality noise: https://status.netprov.example/incidents/2026-03-18
Ops-bot: provider reported route flaps affecting multiple prefixes, AS-path churn observed.
Henri: new plan: revert aggressive batching toggle and raise kvcache soft-evict threshold; also add selector hysteresis to avoid sub-second kernel oscillation.
Maya: +1. Can we ship a config patch to the whole POP and keep selector hysteresis flag enabled by default for lon for 24h?
Tomas: rolling patch to lon now (03:28). will monitor.
Raj: after rollout (03:33) cluster-wide p99 back to baseline ~150-180ms, throughput recovered. No further evictions spike.
Tomas: incident mitigation summary: 1) provider BGP flaps triggered cross-host KV locality churn -> huge miss storm, 2) new aggressive-batching + lowered evict threshold amplified tail, 3) kernel selector oscillation further increased per-request variance. Fixes: revert aggressive-batching, increase KV soft-evict threshold, add 500ms hysteresis to kernel selector, and short-term pin on problematic hosts.
SRE-Jen: filing follow-ups: run 24h canary with selector hysteresis, add telemetry for kv miss-induced batching decisions, add automated rollback if p99 > 500ms after config change.
Maya: please link the PRs and postmortem when ready. great cross-team response. :thumbsup:
Tomas: note: keeping incident open for 24h observation. updating #inc-4821. :white_check_mark:
Deploy-bot: deploy rollback/patch applied @commit b2f4e91 (config-only).
Ops-bot: incident status updated: mitigated (03:34).
